lis.profile: Lis — a cool, deadpan, ironic narrator of an adult comedy show about used cars. Low calm voice, dry humor.
lis.notes: Standalone village comedy: a farmer looks for a car using paper ads on a pole and a newspaper, always late, until a bot finds one in a second. Deadpan, dry irony; numbers said fully. «Перехват» is the name of a bot. Say «Прадо» as «ПРА-до».

fedor.profile: Fyodor — a calm, solid Russian village farmer in his 40s with a beard and a cap, slow deep voice, a bit grumpy, dry humor.
fedor.notes: Line 1: grumpy, tired sigh at a notice board. Line 2: shocked, disbelieving. Line 3: sly, bargaining. Line 4: calm, satisfied, deadpan punchline.

grisha.profile: Grisha — a cheerful, chatty Russian village postman in his 30s on a bicycle, loud, friendly, a bit clueless.
grisha.notes: Line 1: cheerful, then a little embarrassed. Line 2: excited, proud of the news.

savva.profile: Savva — a smart, ironic Russian teenager of 17, the farmer's nephew, a bit cheeky, tech-savvy.

mitrich.profile: Mitrich — an old, kind Russian village neighbour in his 60s in an ushanka, hoarse warm voice, sly and funny.
mitrich.notes: Line 1: surprised, friendly, over the fence early in the morning; say «Федька» very clearly: «ФЕДЬ-ка». Line 2: matter-of-fact, a bit proud of his grandson. Line 3: cheerful, sly bargaining.
